foil.title: Energy repricing risk from Red Sea maritime disruption state
foil.scenario_short: Red Sea maritime disruption will sustain energy repricing over 30d, driven by 64% pressure and 79% state confirmation of an energy supply shock, with 6 urgent critical signals reinforcing the path.
foil.perspective_strategic: The 64% pressure and 79% state confirmation indicate a stable but elevated risk of energy repricing, with the strongest transmission path running through energy supply shock toward Energy.
foil.perspective_contrarian: Counter-evidence includes the IEA's oil market surplus forecast and the second weekly decline in oil prices, which could stall repricing if supply concerns ease and no new hard signals emerge.
foil.actor_lens: Commodity traders: Price whether stress in Red Sea becomes durable over the 30d. Rebalance positions if the probability path moves away from 68%.
foil.top_signal: Red Sea maritime disruption state is feeding energy repricing through energy supply shock, with 64% pressure and 79% state confirmation

This is the honest inverse: for an observed natural-hazard fact, the sourced record IS the only trustworthy source.
